title: Grade 6 Science — Wed, Jun 25
description: Light, Shadows and Reflections — Day 3 of 5: Reflection of light — laws, plane mirrors, images
subject: science

questions.question: Reflection of light means:
options: Light being absorbed by a surface
Light bouncing back from a surface and changing direction
Light bending as it enters a new medium
questions.explanation: Reflection: when light hits a surface and bounces back. All objects reflect some light — that's how we see them. A smooth surface (mirror) reflects light in an ordered way (specular reflection); rough surfaces scatter it (diffuse reflection).

questions.question: The first law of reflection states:
options: The reflected ray bends toward the normal
The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (∠i = ∠r)
questions.explanation: First law: ∠i = ∠r (angle of incidence = angle of reflection). Both angles are measured from the normal (perpendicular to mirror surface at the point of incidence). Second law: incident ray, normal, and reflected ray are all in the same plane.

questions.question: What is the 'normal' in the context of reflection?
options: A perpendicular line drawn at the point of incidence on the reflecting surface
questions.explanation: The normal is an imaginary perpendicular line (90° to the mirror surface) at the exact point where the incident ray hits. Angles of incidence and reflection are always measured from this normal, NOT from the mirror surface.

questions.question: If the angle of incidence is 35°, the angle of reflection is:
questions.explanation: ∠i = ∠r = 35°. The first law of reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.

questions.question: A plane mirror forms an image that is:
options: Virtual, erect (upright), and same size as the object — located as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
questions.explanation: Plane mirror image properties: (1) Virtual (cannot be formed on screen). (2) Erect (right-side up). (3) Same size as object. (4) Laterally inverted (left-right reversed). (5) Image distance = object distance (behind mirror).

questions.question: Lateral inversion in a plane mirror means:
options: Left and right are reversed — your right hand appears as the left hand in the mirror
questions.explanation: Lateral inversion: left-right reversal. When you raise your right hand, your mirror image appears to raise its LEFT hand. This is why text appears reversed in a mirror (AMBULANCE is written reversed on the front of the vehicle so it reads correctly in rear-view mirrors).

questions.question: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a plane mirror. The image is:
options: 15 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation: Plane mirror: image distance = object distance = 15 cm. Image is 15 cm BEHIND the mirror (virtual). The image is not on a screen — it appears to be behind the mirror.

questions.question: What is specular (regular) reflection?
options: Reflection from a rough surface in all directions
Reflection from a smooth surface where parallel rays remain parallel after reflection — produces a clear, sharp image (mirror, calm water)
Absorption of all light by black surfaces
questions.explanation: Specular reflection: smooth surface → parallel incident rays reflect as parallel reflected rays → clear image. Diffuse reflection: rough surface → parallel rays scatter in many directions → no clear image (matte surfaces, paper, walls).

questions.question: Two plane mirrors are placed at 90° to each other. How many images of an object placed between them will be seen?
questions.explanation: Number of images = (360°/angle) − 1 = (360/90) − 1 = 4 − 1 = 3 images. This formula applies when 360/angle is an even integer.

questions.question: Why is the word 'AMBULANCE' written in reverse on ambulance vehicles?
options: Because of lateral inversion — when the driver in front looks in the rear-view mirror, the laterally inverted text becomes readable: 'AMBULANCE'
questions.explanation: Rear-view mirrors laterally invert text. Writing AMBULANCE reversed on the vehicle front means rear-view mirror inversion restores it to readable form, alerting drivers to let the ambulance pass.

questions.question: Why can we see the reflection of trees and mountains in a still lake?
options: The calm water surface acts as a plane mirror (specular reflection) — it reflects the light from the tree/mountain upward to your eye
Lakes are luminous at certain times
questions.explanation: Still water = smooth surface → specular reflection → mirror-like image. A rough/wavy lake surface → diffuse reflection → no clear reflection. This is why reflections in water are clearer on windless days.

questions.question: A ray of light hits a mirror at an angle of 50° to the mirror surface (not the normal). Angle of reflection =
questions.explanation: Angle to mirror surface = 50°. Angle to NORMAL = 90° − 50° = 40°. So angle of incidence = 40° → angle of reflection = 40°. Remember: angles are measured from the normal, not the mirror.

questions.question: Why is the image in a plane mirror called 'virtual'?
options: It cannot be formed on a screen — it appears to be behind the mirror where no light actually reaches; it's formed by the backward extension of reflected rays
It is smaller than the object
It is produced by a lens
questions.explanation: Virtual image: reflected rays diverge; they appear to come FROM a point behind the mirror. If you place a screen behind the mirror, nothing appears there. In contrast, a REAL image is formed where rays actually converge (like a projector image on a screen).

questions.question: Periscopes use two plane mirrors. What is their purpose?
options: To see objects above or around an obstacle by reflecting light twice through a tube — used in submarines to see above water
questions.explanation: Periscope: two plane mirrors at 45° angles. Light enters at top, reflects 90°, travels down the tube, reflects 90° again, exits to the observer's eye. Used in submarines, trenches, and over crowds. Demonstrates practical application of the laws of reflection.

questions.question: If a plane mirror is tilted by 10°, by how much does the reflected ray rotate?
questions.explanation: When a mirror rotates by θ, the reflected ray rotates by 2θ. So 10° tilt → 20° rotation of reflected ray. This is why galvanometers (measuring small currents) use mirrors on the coil — a small rotation gives a large pointer deflection.
